vBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2231: forbid source-introspection tests (tests that readFileSync src/ and regex it)

plan.title: chore(lint): forbid source-introspection tests (tests that readFileSync src/ and regex it)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

references.label: sibling shrink-only baseline lint (pattern to mirror)

narratives.Problem: Source-introspection tests read a source file's TEXT (readFileSync/readFile of a .ts/.tsx path) and regex-match it instead of exercising runtime behavior. When a refactor moves/renames the source (e.g. the #2124 workspaces decomposition moved routes/workspaces.ts), every such test goes red on main and every branch at once, emptying the merge gate. tests/lib/cloister/review-agent.test.ts (20 reads), SettingsPage.test.ts (11), and ~19 other test files currently do this.
narratives.Proposal: Add scripts/lint-source-introspection.sh (modeled on lint-file-size.sh) wired into `npm run lint`. It fails when a test file passes a .ts/.tsx string-literal path to readFileSync/readFile. Existing offenders are captured in a committed, enumerable, shrink-only baseline scripts/source-introspection-baseline.txt seeded by the script's own --regen (so baseline==scanner output and CI is green on the seed commit). A self-test proves the guard bites on a new offender and passes clean. Detection is multi-line aware and matches both root-relative ('src/....ts') and test-relative ('../../x.tsx') literals (NOT a 'src/' substring match, which would miss the largest cluster).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Repointing existing offenders to behavioral assertions or exported constants (deferred 'over time' per the issue).
- Detecting dynamically-computed (non-literal) source paths.
- Flagging reads of non-source fixtures (.json/.md/.yaml/.jsonl) or a test reading its own generated output.
- Deleting or refactoring routes/workspaces.ts or any existing offender test file.

autoDecisions.summary: Detection = a .ts/.tsx string literal read in a test file, NOT a 'src/'-substring match.
autoDecisions.rationale: The largest offender cluster (SettingsPage.test.ts, 11 reads) uses test-relative '../../*.tsx' paths with no 'src/' substring; the extension signal is the correct generalization and yields near-zero false positives (tests exercise behavior via import, not readFileSync).

autoDecisions.summary: Baseline metric = per-file offender count, shrink-only ratchet, mirroring scripts/file-size-baseline.txt.
autoDecisions.rationale: Well-understood, already-tested pattern (lint-file-size.sh); baselined count may drop (stale -> --update) but never rise; unbaselined file with count>0 fails.

autoDecisions.summary: --regen is the seed + audited-accept path; baseline is seeded by the script's own scanner.
autoDecisions.rationale: Guarantees baseline==scanner output on the seed commit so `check` passes deterministically in CI, and keeps detection logic DRY in one place.

autoDecisions.summary: Script + seed baseline + lint-chain wiring ship as ONE bead.
autoDecisions.rationale: An unwired guard never runs in CI (zero value) and an unbaselined guard cannot pass its own check; they are atomically coupled into one working, CI-enforced tracer-bullet slice.

autoDecisions.summary: Repointing existing offenders is out of scope.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue defers it explicitly; acceptance requires only that new offenders fail lint and existing ones are baselined and enumerable.

items.title: Add lint-source-introspection.sh guard, seed shrink-only baseline, and wire into the lint chain

expected_outputs: scripts/lint-source-introspection.sh exits 0 on the seed commit (all current offenders baselined), printing a '✓' pass line

scripts/source-introspection-baseline.txt exists, is sorted by path, and contains one '<count> <path>' line per current offender including tests/lib/cloister/review-agent.test.ts and src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/Settings/__tests__/SettingsPage.test.ts
npm run lint:source-introspection is present in package.json scripts and appears in the `lint` chain

narrative.Action: Create scripts/lint-source-introspection.sh following scripts/lint-file-size.sh conventions (bash, `set -euo pipefail`, `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`, `<count> <path>` baseline sorted by path, `✓`/`✗` messages with an actionable remediation line). Scanner: over test files matching tests/**/*.ts(x), src/**/__tests__/**/*.ts(x), src/**/*.test.ts(x), count per-file occurrences of a readFileSync/readFile call whose path argument is a single- or double-quoted string literal ending in `.ts` or `.tsx`. Detection MUST be multi-line aware (call token and path literal may be on adjacent lines) — mirror the windowed awk/perl scan in scripts/lint-state-writes.sh; do NOT require a literal 'src/' substring. Modes: default `check` (fail on new offender file, on count increase over baseline, and on stale/removed baseline entries — pointing to --update); `--update` (recompute counts for existing baseline entries only: lower stale, drop resolved/removed, never raise/add); `--regen` (write the full current offender set — the one-time seed and audited accept-new-offender path). Seed scripts/source-introspection-baseline.txt by running `--regen` (never hand-write it), then confirm default `check` exits 0. Add `"lint:source-introspection": "bash scripts/lint-source-introspection.sh"` to package.json scripts and append `&& npm run lint:source-introspection` to the `lint` chain adjacent to `lint:file-size`. Touch ONLY scripts/ and package.json — do NOT edit any existing offender *.test.ts(x) file.

items.title: Given the seed commit, when `bash scripts/lint-source-introspection.sh` runs, it exits 0 and prints a '✓' pass line (baseline equals the scanner's own output).

The committed scripts/source-introspection-baseline.txt contains one '<count> <path>' line per current offender, sorted by path — and contains tests/lib/cloister/review-agent.test.ts and src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/Settings/__tests__/SettingsPage.test.ts (the multi-line-read file).

When a test file reads a root-relative ('src/....ts') literal, a test-relative ('../../x.tsx') literal, or the multi-line `readFileSync(\n  '../x.tsx')` form, the scanner produces a violation for it — a literal 'src/' substring is not required.
Given package.json contains a `lint:source-introspection` script in the `lint` chain, when `npm run lint` runs against a tree with an unbaselined offender, it exits non-zero.

When a baselined file's offending-read count decreases, `check` exits non-zero (stale) and `--update` produces a lowered baseline count and drops resolved/removed entries; `--update` never raises a count or adds an entry, and `--regen` produces the full current offender set.
Add self-test proving the guard fails on a new introspection read, passes clean, and ratchets on --update

expected_outputs: the test covers: new-offender-fails (incl. a multi-line read fixture), clean-tree-passes, and --update-ratchets-down

narrative.Action: Create tests/unit/scripts/lint-source-introspection.test.ts modeled on tests/unit/scripts/lint-file-size.test.ts (execFileSync/spawnSync, a temp workspace, install-the-script, write baseline, runLint -> {ok, output}). Cases: (1) a clean temp tree with an empty/matching baseline exits 0; (2) a test file with a single-line `readFileSync(join(cwd, 'src/foo.ts'))` and no baseline entry exits non-zero and names the offender; (3) a test file with the MULTI-LINE `readFileSync(\n  '../foo.tsx'),` form is detected (guards against the line-scoped-grep miss, hazard H2); (4) a baselined file whose offending-read count DROPS is reported stale in `check` and is ratcheted down by `--update`; (5) `--update` never raises a count or adds a new file. Use vi.useFakeTimers only if any delay is involved (none expected here). Do not touch scripts/ or package.json — test only.

items.title: Given a temp test file with a new unbaselined `.ts` source read, when the script runs in check mode, it exits non-zero and the output names the offending file.
Given a temp test file using the multi-line `readFileSync(\n  '../foo.tsx')` form, the scanner detects it (exits non-zero) — proving multi-line awareness.
Given a clean temp tree whose baseline matches, when the script runs in check mode, it exits 0.
Given a baselined file whose offending-read count decreases, `check` reports it stale and `--update` lowers the baseline count (and never raises or adds).
